tagline: Twelve paved miles up to a tarn under the cliffs.
intro: Angel Lake Road starts in Wells, just south of I-80, and climbs about 12 miles into the East Humboldt Range, the last of it by switchbacks up the steep eastern face. Clover Valley drops away below. Above, the range runs up to Greys Peak at 10,674 feet.
The Forest Service counts it the only paved road in the area to an alpine lake.

moments.title: Wells
moments.text: The town began as Humboldt Wells, near the springs where the Humboldt River starts, and got its short name after an 1877 telegraph that said only that Wells was burning.

moments.title: The switchbacks
moments.text: On the way up the road shows the work of the ice ages, U-shaped canyons, moraines and steeply carved granite cliffs and cirques.

moments.title: Angel Lake
moments.text: The road ends at 8,378 feet beside a 13-acre tarn under cirque cliffs, named not for any angel but for Warren M. Angel, an early Clover Valley rancher.

practical: The road may be closed in winter, and the campground at the lake is generally open from Memorial Day to Labor Day.
